config._note: HR/labour approval record (urenstaat). hrmq-hours-process-redesign (design.md Decision 8): the Timesheet is now the period AGGREGATE of TimeEntry bookings, so (1) the total-hours KPI stat sums the TRUTH — TimeEntry.hours filtered on timesheetId = @objectId — not the cached Timesheet.hours field; (2) the 'Urenstaat' data widget shows the aggregate facts (period/hours/entryCount/description/billable) with everything but the timesheet-level description read-only (hours/entryCount are server-recomputed aggregates, REQ-TEC-004). description is the ONLY page-editable field: the design's page-level includeFields [description] edit allowlist is expressed through this widget's editable overrides, because CnDetailPage has no page-level includeFields prop — a config key no component reads is a comment, so none is declared; (3) the 'Goedkeuring' panel (status/submittedAt/approvedBy/approvedAt/rejectionReason) is fully read-only — process fields are lifecycle-stamped server-side and inert to client input; (4) the new 'Urenboekingen' object-list lists the TimeEntry bookings (timesheetId = @objectId), rowRoute to TimeEntryDetail — entry mutability is governed server-side by the parent's state (REQ-TEC-005). Related resolves the claiming Employee (employeeId excluded from data widgets). Files keeps approval evidence full-width on the body. NO email/calendar/talk widgets — the Timesheet schema declares no comms linkedTypes; any communication is with the person (Employee), not the record. lifecycleActions expose the schema's own submit/approve/reject/reopen transitions (guarded server-side by NoSelfApprovalGuard, and TimesheetNotEmptyGuard on submit). Audit history stays a sidebar tab as a rarely-scanned surface.

hrmq-hours-process-redesign (design.md Decision 8): MijnUren is the self-service BOOKING surface and now lists TimeEntry (the individual booking), not Timesheet (the period aggregate). Converted from an indexScaffold pageInstance to a concrete page because the create-form allowlist keys (includeFields/fieldOverrides) are not indexScaffold params, and widening the shared template for one page is worse than an explicit page (the template file's own 80%-fit rule). Add is enabled via actionToggles.showAdd — NEVER the dead allowCreate key (not a CnIndexPage prop; fleet anti-pattern 11). includeFields is the exact self-service allowlist: the employee's own Employee record, userId, administrationId and costCenter are resolved/stamped server-side by TimeEntryStampListener, and hours is derived from start/end/break — none of them may appear on the form (spec: 'The booking form is an allowlist'). fieldOverrides orders billable last (times → break → what → project → billable).
config.description: Log your hours and see your own time entries.
config._fieldOrderNote: Field order is declared once on the TimeEntry SCHEMA (property `order`: start 10, end 20, break 30, description 40, project 50, billable 60), not per page — fieldsFromSchema sorts by overrides.order > prop.order > ALPHABETICAL, so a schema with no order renders every form as an alphabetical wall. That is exactly what happened here: the booking form showed End before Start (breakMinutes, description, endedAt, projectId, startedAt), which the e2e caught by filling the two datetime inputs positionally and getting a span the server correctly refused. Declaring order on the schema fixes every surface at once; no page-level override is needed.

params.title: Timesheets
params.note: hrmq-hours-process-redesign (design.md Decision 8): timesheets are server-created period aggregates of TimeEntry bookings, so Add and inline edit are disabled (actionToggles — never the dead allowCreate key); columns show the aggregate facts (hours/entryCount) instead of the retired per-period billable flag. Row click opens TimesheetDetail.

params.title: Timesheet approval
params.description: Submitted timesheets awaiting approval or rejection — open a timesheet to approve or reject it.
params.note: hrmq-hours-process-redesign (design.md Decision 8): the approval queue is a read-only worklist — Add/edit/delete are disabled (aggregates are server-created; approve/reject happen through the lifecycle actions on TimesheetDetail, guarded server-side by NoSelfApprovalGuard). Filters/defaultFilters/sort unchanged.

params.title: Team timesheet approval
params.description: Submitted timesheets from your team awaiting approval or rejection (mss-team-scope) — based on the managerUserId link derived from the organisational structure.
params.note: hrmq-hours-process-redesign (design.md Decision 8): same read-only worklist deltas as TimesheetApproval; the managerUserId: @me base filter is untouched — since this change, managerUserId is a server-maintained cache of the org chain (OrgAssignment → OrgUnit.managerId), stamped by TimesheetProcessStampListener via the shared OrgResolutionService, so the queue follows the org structure rather than hand-entered data.
